prompt: CSSFontFeatureValuesMap set method exception too many values
answer:
`CSSFontFeatureValuesMap.set()` accepts either one unsigned integer or a sequence of unsigned integers. However, some feature-value blocks impose a maximum number of values.

For `characterVariant`, the value must contain no more than two integers. Passing more than two causes the method to throw an `InvalidAccessError`:

```js
rule.characterVariant.set("alpha-2", [1, 2, 3]);
// InvalidAccessError
```

The CSS Fonts specification states that `set()` throws `InvalidAccessError` when the input sequence contains more values than the associated feature-value block allows. A single integer is treated as a one-value sequence. (W3C CSS Fonts Module Level 4: https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/WD-css-fonts-4-20260906/)
